content:
Today is September 1st, and Apple officially handed over the position of Chief Executive Officer from Tim Cook to John Ternus, marking the official start of a new era led by Ternus.

The change can be seen on the company's updated leadership page — Ternus has been given the title of Chief Executive Officer, while Cook has moved to the board of directors section, appearing under the new title of 'Executive Chairman'.

Ternus's rise to the top signals a shift in company strategy. Compared with Cook's strength in operations management, Ternus will bring a more product-centric vision. However, these changes will take time to implement gradually. His first public appearance will be at the company's autumn launch event, where he will introduce the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra product lines, with the event scheduled for September 9th.

Previously, the board members listed on the leadership website only showed their names. With Cook joining the board, Apple has also expanded this section by adding individual profile photos of each member.

Board members include Tim Cook, Arthur Levinson, Wanda Austin, Alex Gorsky, Andrea Jung, Monica Lozano, Ron Sugar, Sue Wagner, and John Ternus, who occupies a seat as Chief Executive Officer.
